fi-ancistrus-cf-cirrhosus.title: Bristlenose Pleco
fi-ancistrus-cf-cirrhosus.summary: The common bristlenose catfish, Ancistrus sp. '3', is the loricariid sold everywhere as the 'bristlenose', of unknown origin and bred commercially. It was once thought close to the Argentinian A.…
rows: Does best when offered a varied diet comprising sinking dried foods, frozen Daphnia, mosquito larvae, chironomid larvae (bloodworm), and prawn/shrimp, for, example, plus some fresh fruit, parboiled potato, etc.
notes: Compared to some others in the genus it's largely undemanding, but does prefer well-oxygenated water.
Provided there is plenty of cover décor is largely unimportant.

fi-dekeyseria-brachyura.title: Butterfly Pleco L52
fi-dekeyseria-brachyura.summary: The butterfly plec, Dekeyseria brachyura (L168), is a flattened loricariid catfish from the Rio Negro in Brazil. Also called the chameleon plec, it changes colour to match the substrate and other…
rows: Primarily vegetarian, so the bulk of the diet should be composed of vegetable matter in both fresh (cucumber slices, blanched spinach etc.) and dried (algae wafers, spirulina tablets etc.) forms.
notes: This species needs well-oxygenated water, preferably with a high degree of movement.
Provide lots of cover in the form of driftwood roots and branches, and if you wish, smooth rocks and plants.

fi-leporacanthicus-joselimai.title: Leporacanthicus joselimai
fi-leporacanthicus-joselimai.summary: The sultan plec, Leporacanthicus joselimai (L264), is a suckermouth catfish from the Rio Tapajós in Brazil. It lives in rapids and other fast-flowing waters among rocks and driftwood snags. Young…
rows: These prefer a meaty diet, which can consist of live and frozen foods such as bloodworm, chopped mussel and prawn and sinking dried foods.
notes: A spacious tank is required, preferably with a sandy substrate.
Provide hiding places and shade with some big chunks of driftwood and smooth rocks.

fi-ancistrus-ranunculus.title: Medusa Pleco L034
fi-ancistrus-ranunculus.summary: Ancistrus ranunculus, the medusa pleco (L034), is a wide-headed, flattened suckermouth catfish from the rio Xingu and rio Tocantins basins in Brazil. It lives among rocks in shallow, fast-flowing…
rows: Prefers a more protein-rich diet than the majority of Ancistrus spp., so supplement quality, sinking dried foods with regular offerings of live and frozen foods such as bloodworm, chopped mussel, prawn and similar.
Rio Xingu and rio Tocantins basins, Brazil.
notes: A stream-type setup with a gravel or sand substrate and rounded stones and rocks would simulate its natural biotope, but it's equally at home in a planted tank.
It does need well-oxygenated water with a lot of movement, though, and live plants tend not to do so well under these conditions.

fi-baryancistrus-chrysolomus.title: King Pleco L047
fi-baryancistrus-chrysolomus.summary: The mango pleco, Baryancistrus chrysolomus, traded as L047, is a loricariid endemic to the rio Xingu basin in Pará state, Brazil. A broad, usually yellowish band along the edges of the dorsal and…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates

Herbivore / algae browser. Gut analyses of wild specimens revealed the diet to be composed chiefly of algae, particularly diatoms and filamentous genera such as Spirogyra alongside smaller amounts of invertebrates such as…
Endemic to the rio Xingu basin in Pará state, Brazil, where it inhabits a section of the river's main channel known as 'Volta Grande do rio Xingu' directly above Belo Monte falls.
notes: Not difficult to maintain under the correct conditions but largely unsuitable for the 'general' community aquarium.
We recommend keeping it in a set-up designed to resemble a flowing river with a substrate of variably-sized rocks, gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-baryancistrus-xanthellus.title: Gold Nugget Pleco L018
fi-baryancistrus-xanthellus.summary: The gold nugget pleco, Baryancistrus xanthellus, is a suckermouth catfish endemic to the rio Xingu basin in Pará state, Brazil. It lives in whitewater rapids in the Volta Grande do rio Xingu, between…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates

Herbivore / algae browser. Gut analyses of wild specimens revealed the diet to be composed chiefly of algae, particularly diatoms and filamentous genera such as Spirogyra alongside smaller amounts of invertebrates such as…
Endemic to the rio Xingu basin where it inhabits a section of the river's main channel known as 'Volta Grande do rio Xingu' which lies between Belo Monte falls and the mouth of…
notes: Not difficult to maintain under the correct conditions but largely unsuitable for the 'general' community aquarium.
We recommend keeping it in a set-up designed to resemble a flowing river with a substrate of variably-sized rocks, gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-ancistrus-triradiatus.title: Staghorn Bristlenose LDA72
fi-ancistrus-triradiatus.summary: The horned bristlenose pleco, Ancistrus triradiatus, is a small suckermouth catfish from Colombia and Venezuela, found among rocks in flowing streams. It is often confused with the common…
rows: Herbivore / algae browser. Mainly vegetarian, so the bulk of the diet should be composed of vegetable matter in both fresh (cucumber slices, blanched spinach etc.) and dried (algae wafers, Spirulina tablets etc.) forms.
notes: A stream-type setup with a gravel or sand substrate and rounded stones and rocks would simulate its natural biotope, but it's equally at home in a planted tank.
It does require well-oxygenated water, however, and live plants tend not to do so well under these conditions.

fi-pterygoplichthys-gibbiceps.title: Albino Gibbiceps Pleco L165
fi-pterygoplichthys-gibbiceps.summary: Pterygoplichthys gibbiceps [ 2 ] is a species of armored catfish native to Brazil, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela, where it is found in the Orinoco and Amazon basins.
rows: Up to about 50.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-hypostomus-plecostomus.title: Albino Chocolate Pleco
fi-hypostomus-plecostomus.summary: Acipenser plecostomus Linnaeus, 1758 Hypostomus guacari Lacepède, 1803 Loricaria flava Shaw, 1804 Plecostomus bicirrosus Gronow, 1854 Plecostomus brasiliensis Bleeker, 1864 Plecostomus plecostomus…
rows: Up to about 25.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-panaque-nigrolineatus.title: Watermelon Pleco L330
fi-panaque-nigrolineatus.summary: Watermelon Pleco L330 (Panaque nigrolineatus) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 43.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)
notes: [ edit ] The royal panaque can be found in the Orinoco River and a number of tributaries of the Amazon River.

fi-peckoltia-brevis.title: Peckoltia Brevis Pleco LDA078 Anama
fi-peckoltia-brevis.summary: Peckoltia brevis is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Loricariidae, the suckermouth armoured catfishes, and the subfamily Hypostominae, the suckermouth catfishes. This…
rows: Up to about 11.4 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-peckoltia-vittata.title: Bumblebee Pleco L015
fi-peckoltia-vittata.summary: Peckoltia vittata is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Loricariidae, the suckermouth armoured catfishes, and the subfamily Hypostominae, the suckermouth catfishes.…
rows: Up to about 15.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-hemiancistrus-sabaji.title: Para Pleco L075
fi-hemiancistrus-sabaji.summary: Peckoltia sabaji is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Loricariidae, the suckermouth armoured catfishes, and the subfamily Hypostominae, the suckermouth catfishes. [ 2…
rows: Up to about 19.8 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-ancistrus-brevifilis.title: Ancistrus Brevifilis Pleco L149
fi-ancistrus-brevifilis.summary: Ancistrus brevifilis is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Loricariidae, the suckermouth armoured catfishes, and the subfamily Hypostominae, the suckermouth catfishes.…
rows: Up to about 11.8 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-hypostomus-faveolus.title: Snakeskin Pleco L037
fi-hypostomus-faveolus.summary: Hypostomus faveolus [ 1 ] is a species of catfish in the family Loricariidae. It is native to South America, where it occurs in the basins of the Tocantins River and the Xingu River in central…
rows: Up to about 20.6 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-panaqolus-albivermis.title: Flash Pleco (L204)
fi-panaqolus-albivermis.summary: A small wood-eating pleco from Peru with pale, worm-like stripes, known in the trade as L204. Needs plenty of bogwood to chew on.
rows: About 4 in (9.6 cm SL, FishBase); some keepers report up to about 6 in
Wood eater: plenty of bogwood, plus algae wafers, catfish pellets, granules and some frozen foods
San Alejandro River, upper Ucayali drainage, Peru
notes: Use a mature tank with lots of bogwood and sheltered caves; keep the light dim to medium.
IUCN lists it as Endangered: it comes from one small area that is heavily collected for the trade.

sources.name: Maidenhead Aquatics fishkeeper.co.uk – Flash Plec L204

fi-l243.title: Banded Peckoltia Pleco (L243)
fi-l243.summary: A small, boldly patterned suckermouth catfish from the upper Orinoco in southern Venezuela, with orange-yellow markings on a dark body. A peaceful algae and biofilm grazer that wants strong, clean, well-oxygenated flow and plenty of rock caves.
rows: About 4–5 in (Seriously Fish 120 mm SL; Aquarist Atlas about 10.5 cm SL)
Peaceful with other fish; males squabble over caves, so give extra caves if keeping more than one
Grazer: algae wafers and spirulina sinking foods with blanched vegetables, plus an occasional meaty food. Driftwood to rasp is welcome, though it is not a wood-eater
Upper Río Orinoco drainage (Ventuari River), Amazonas state, southern Venezuela
notes: Build rock caves and narrow crevices; it hides by day and comes out at dusk.
Needs strong filtration and good oxygen: it comes from fast, clear water.
Often exported mixed with the similar Peckoltia lineola.

fi-panaqolus-tankei.title: Tankei Tiger Pleco (L398)
fi-panaqolus-tankei.summary: A small, tiger-striped wood-eating pleco from the Rio Xingu in Brazil, described in 2016. It needs plenty of driftwood to rasp, shady caves, and clean, oxygen-rich water with a good current.
rows: About 5.5–6 in (14–15 cm); Wikipedia gives 8.3 cm standard length
Peaceful toward other fish; males squabble over territory
Can be kept singly or in a small group with extra caves
Wood-eater: driftwood must be in the tank. Add vegetables (zucchini, cucumber, sweet potato) with algae wafers and sinking catfish pellets; avoid regular high-protein feeding
notes: Give it a mature tank with lots of bogwood, smooth rocks and dim, shaded areas; it is nocturnal.
Strong filtration is needed to handle the wood waste it produces.
Tie hardy plants such as Anubias or Java fern to the wood; soft plants get eaten or uprooted.

sources.name: Maidenhead Aquatics fishkeeper.co.uk – Tankei Tiger Plec L398

fi-hypancistrus-l260.title: Queen Arabesque Pleco (L260)
fi-hypancistrus-l260.summary: A small black-and-white maze-patterned pleco from Brazil's Rio Tapajós. Peaceful and suited to a flowing, rocky tank with lots of caves; it prefers meaty foods.
rows: Peaceful; does not compete well with aggressive or very territorial fish
Omnivore leaning to meaty foods: sinking pellets, frozen daphnia, bloodworm and shrimp; some vegetables may be taken
Moderate: needs a mature, stable tank
notes: Set up a stream-style tank with rocks, sand, driftwood and caves, good flow and plenty of oxygen.
Do not keep with other Hypancistrus species: they can hybridize.

fi-hypancistrus-l333.title: Black & White Royal Tiger Pleco (L333)
fi-hypancistrus-l333.sci: Hypancistrus sp. (L333; often given as H. seideli)
fi-hypancistrus-l333.summary: A black-and-yellow or black-and-white patterned pleco from the Rio Xingu in Brazil. Peaceful, it likes warm, fast, oxygen-rich water and a mostly meaty diet.
rows: Mostly meaty: bloodworm, chopped mussel and prawn, sinking pellets; vegetables rarely eaten
notes: Set up a stream-style tank with rocks, sand, driftwood, caves and strong flow.
Do not keep with other Hypancistrus species: they can hybridize.

fi-ancistomus-l147.title: Head Spotted Peckoltia (L147)
fi-ancistomus-l147.summary: A spotted suckermouth catfish from the middle Orinoco in Venezuela and Colombia. It needs a roomy tank with caves and warm, clean water.
rows: Venezuela and Colombia: tributaries of the middle Río Orinoco
notes: Give each pleco its own cave or hiding spot.

fi-hemiancistrus-guahiborum.title: Orange Seam Pleco (L106)
fi-hemiancistrus-guahiborum.summary: A dark pleco with orange-edged fins from the Orinoco. A decent community fish that likes current and well-oxygenated water and eats a mix of foods.
rows: Peaceful; give each fish its own refuge
Omnivore: sinking dried foods plus bloodworm and daphnia
notes: Needs well-oxygenated water with some current; a stream-style tank with rounded stones suits it.

fi-hemiancistrus-l128.title: Blue Phantom Pleco (L128)
fi-hemiancistrus-l128.summary: A dark green-black pleco with blue spots from the Orinoco basin. It grows to about 8 in and likes warm water with some current and a mix of plant and meaty foods.
rows: Peaceful; a little territorial with its own kind
Omnivore: vegetable foods plus varied sinking foods
notes: May be a northern form of the similar green phantom pleco (L200).
Give it caves, driftwood and moderate current.

sources.name: Practical Fishkeeping – Blue phantom plec, L128

fi-panaque-l191.title: Royal Pleco (L191, Dull-eyed Royal Pleco)
fi-panaque-l191.summary: A big wood-eating royal pleco from Colombia. It needs driftwood to chew, strong filtration and eventually a 6 ft tank.
rows: About 12–16 in (30–40 cm); listed to 20 in (500 mm SL)
About 6 ft (180 cm) long when fully grown
Peaceful with other fish; can be territorial with its own kind
Wood eater: needs driftwood to rasp, plus cucumber, zucchini and sinking tablets
notes: Produces a lot of waste: use a large filter turning the tank over about six times an hour, with good flow.
Hides by day and feeds at night.
warn: Grows large and lives a long time; plan for a big tank.

fi-peckoltia-l103.title: Clown Pleco (L103)
fi-peckoltia-l103.summary: A small banded pleco from the Orinoco near Puerto Ayacucho, Venezuela. Peaceful and easy to fit in, it likes driftwood, caves and warm water.
rows: About 32 in (80 cm) long or larger
Peaceful; may be territorial over caves
Can be kept singly or in small groups
Omnivore: sinking wafers, vegetables and some meaty foods; grazes driftwood
Venezuela: Río Orinoco basin near Puerto Ayacucho
notes: Provide driftwood and a cave for each pleco.

fi-chaetostoma-l146.title: Albino Rubber Lip Pleco (L146a)
fi-chaetostoma-l146.summary: An albino form of the rubber lip pleco, a stream-dwelling algae grazer. It prefers cooler, very clean, oxygen-rich water with current.
rows: Mostly plant-based: algae, biofilm, algae wafers and blanched vegetables
notes: Needs high oxygen and good water flow; avoid very warm tanks.

fi-chaetostoma-sacramento.title: Tiger Rubber Lip Pleco (L455)
fi-chaetostoma-sacramento.summary: A boldly patterned rubbernose pleco from Peru (L455, L456 and L457 are the same species) that grazes algae in fast, oxygen-rich water. Best in a tank with good flow and supplemental vegetable foods.
rows: Algae grazer: biofilm, algae wafers, spirulina and blanched vegetables like cucumber, zucchini and lettuce; also takes tablets and worm foods
Peru: fast, rocky streams of the Pampa del Sacramento region
notes: Needs strong water flow, a sand bottom and plenty of hiding places.
